words.where: Mexico, Argentina, Uruguay, much of Central America

note: Means to fuck. In the Caribbean, Colombia and Spain it's a harmless word for take or grab, so people from those places often get caught out. Use tomar or agarrar.
Means penis. Everywhere else it's just a bug or a critter, so this one surprises a lot of visitors.
Slang for female genitals, which is why Cubans say fruta bomba for the fruit.
Slang for female genitals. Concha de tu madre is a strong insult. Elsewhere it's a seashell, and in Mexico also a sweet bread.

words.where: Cuba, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Spain

note: Literally female genitals. In practice it's a very common swear word for surprise or anger, like damn or fuck. It's in everyday speech but still rude in polite company.
Slang for female genitals, and ¡chucha! works as an exclamation. In Colombia it means armpit odor instead.
Means penis. Vete a la verga is roughly fuck off, and ¡verga! alone is a strong exclamation.
Means penis. In Cuba, de pinga can mean either awesome or awful, depending on tone.
Means penis. Elsewhere it's a beak or a peak. Chileans say hora punta rather than hora pico for rush hour.
Means penis. In Chile and Colombia it's a betting pool or lottery, so context matters.
Means penis. In Spain, pijo and pija describe a snobby rich kid, which isn't vulgar.
Means to fuck, and it's the root of a whole family of Mexican swearing. Chingada is a strong insult, while chingón means awesome and is much milder.
Means no way or you're kidding. It's very common among friends, but mamar refers to oral sex here, so don't say it to your boss or your in-laws. No manches is the clean version.
From chingar. Means badass or awesome: ¡qué chingón! Very common among friends, but vulgar, so not for school, work or grandparents. Chido and padre say the same politely.
A shitload, a ton: tengo un chingo de trabajo. Vulgar; un montón or mucho say the same.
Confusingly, it can mean awesome (la fiesta estuvo poca madre) or shameless (¡qué poca madre!, how low can you get). Vulgar either way, because anything about someone's mother is strong in Mexico.
A huge mess or a wild time: la fiesta fue un desmadre. Rude but very common. Relajo, lío or caos are polite.
Laziness or boredom: me da hueva levantarme, I can't be bothered to get up. From huevo, slang for testicle, so it's crude. Flojera says the same politely.
Honestly, for real: al chile, no me gustó. Chile is also slang for penis, so it's crude. En serio or la verdad are safe.
Dude or man among friends: ¿qué onda, güey? Young Mexicans say it constantly, but it started as an insult meaning fool, from buey, ox, and it's still rude toward someone you don't know.
Tacky or low-class. It's classist and often racist, aimed at poorer and Indigenous people, so it hurts more than it sounds. Better not to use it.

Literally to fuck. In Spain it's an everyday swear word. In the Caribbean, no jodas is closer to quit messing around, or no way. It's milder there, but still not polite. Jodido means fucked or screwed (estoy jodido, I'm screwed) and also very hard, and ¡jódete! is fuck you or tough luck. In Argentina and Uruguay, una joda is just a party or a joke.
Means whore. It's an insult aimed at someone's mother or at women, which is why it hits hard. ¡Puta! alone is also an exclamation.
Literally a big male goat, with an old sense of a man whose wife cheats on him. It means bastard, but among close male friends it can mean dude. Tone decides, so don't try it yourself.
Literally a pubic hair. It means idiot, and it's stronger than tonto. In Argentina it just means a kid, and is much milder.
Both come from words for testicles and mean idiot. Among friends they're also the everyday word for dude, so you'll hear them constantly. With strangers they're an insult.
Culo means ass and mierda means shit. They carry about the same weight as the English words, and both are understood everywhere.

words.where: everywhere, with a casual sense in Colombia

note: A slur against gay men, and offensive in the same way as its English equivalents. Colombian friends may call each other marica to mean dude, but that doesn't make it safe for a learner to copy. Say gay or homosexual.
Means to fuck. In Chile and much of Central America it's everyday slang for catch or get it (¿cachai?), so a Chilean saying it in Lima can get an awkward laugh.
Means tits or boobs. Crude, about like the English. Pechos or senos are the neutral words, and teta is fine for breastfeeding (darle la teta al bebé).

Means balls (testicles), and also guts or nerve: tener cojones, to have the guts. Very common in Spain as an exclamation of surprise or anger. Huevos is the Latin American equivalent, and valor or agallas are the clean words for courage.

words.where: Mexico, Spain, much of Latin America

note: In Mexico and much of Latin America it's a slur against gay men, as offensive as maricón; it's the chant FIFA has fined Mexico's fans for. In Spain el puto coche is the fucking car, a crude intensifier.

Means to shit. Crude, about like the English. Cagarla is to screw up (la cagué, I blew it). In Spain, me cago en… followed by something sacred is a very strong curse. Hacer caca is the word for children, and ir al baño the polite one.
Means to piss. Crude but very common in Spain. Hacer pis is the everyday word, and orinar the formal one.
Means to fuck, and it's the usual crude word in Spain. Latin America says coger or culear instead, so follar there sounds Spanish, but it's understood.

words.where: everywhere, especially the Caribbean, Venezuela, Colombia, the Southern Cone and Spain

note: An old word for penis that now works like damn or hell: ¡carajo!, me importa un carajo (I don't give a damn), vete al carajo (go to hell). Mild in some countries and rude in others, so keep it among friends. ¡Caramba! and ¡caray! are the clean versions.

Means damn, damned or cursed: ¡maldito perro!, ¡maldición! It's mild, and dubbed movies use it far more than people do, since it stands in for English swearing. Calling a person maldito is a real insult, though.

The communion wafer at Mass, so religious people can find the other uses offensive. In Spain ¡hostia! is a very common exclamation of surprise, like holy shit, and dar una hostia is to smack someone. Barely used this way in Latin America.
Comes from coño. De coña means as a joke, or great (lo pasamos de coña), and ni de coña means no way. Casual and a bit crude, not used in Latin America.

words.where: Colombia, Venezuela, Peru: nonsense or lies

note: Paja is straw, which is fine everywhere (una pajita for a drink in Spain). Hacerse una paja is crude slang for masturbating. In Colombia and Venezuela, paja also means nonsense or lies (eso es pura paja), which is milder.

words.es: ¿qué pedo?, estar pedo, no hay pedo

note: A fart, which is a childish, mildly rude word everywhere. In Mexico it's a whole family of slang: ¿qué pedo? is what's up, estar pedo is to be drunk, no hay pedo is no problem, and un pedo is a hassle. Friendly but crude, so not with your boss.
Means idiot. About as strong as the English: fine for a movie character, rude when said to someone. Tonto is milder and can even be affectionate.

Means stupid, but calling a person estúpido is a stronger insult than the English word, closer to calling someone a jerk or moron. Saying something is una idea estúpida is milder. Tonto or bobo is the gentle version.
Means imbecile or moron, stronger than idiota. It was once a medical label for people with intellectual disabilities, which is part of why it stings.
Means cretin or moron. A bit old-fashioned, and much more common in dubbed movies than in speech. Like imbécil, it began as a medical term for a disability.
Means idiot or moron. It comes from tara, a defect, and was used for people with disabilities, so it's more hurtful than it sounds.
A slur for people with intellectual disabilities, like the English r-word. Retrasado for something delayed is perfectly fine: el vuelo viene retrasado. Say persona con discapacidad intelectual.

Cojo is someone with a limp or a missing leg, and manco someone missing a hand or arm. They're the old plain words and not always meant badly (la mesa está coja, the table wobbles), but said about a person they can hurt. Say persona con discapacidad, or describe what you mean: usa muletas, le falta un brazo.

Means dwarf, as in fairy tales. Used for a person of short stature it's offensive, like midget in English; say persona de talla baja. Families also use enano affectionately for a small child, which is fine.
A female dog, which is fine for a dog. Aimed at a woman it means bitch, a strong insult. Spaniards also say estar sin una perra, to be broke, from an old coin.
A female fox, but aimed at a woman it means slut or bitch, a strong insult. Say zorro for the animal in general, as people do in everyday speech.
Means bastard. It's in dubbed movies constantly but less common in real speech. It offends because of its old meaning, a child born outside marriage.

words.where: everywhere, as an insult especially in Mexico and the Caribbean

note: Means wretch or bastard when aimed at someone, and it's a strong insult in Mexico and the Caribbean. In formal writing it can still mean unfortunate (un final desgraciado), and desgraciadamente means unfortunately, which is fine.
Spain's everyday word for idiot or jerk, built on polla, so it's vulgar. Extremely common there and rare in Latin America. Same word for one or many: un gilipollas, unos gilipollas.
A flower bud or a cocoon, which is fine. In Spain it's also slang for foreskin and an insult meaning jerk or dickhead.
Canalla means scoundrel or swine, a bit old-fashioned but strong. Escoria is slag from melting metal, and aimed at people it means scum, said with real contempt.
Means shameless person or rascal. It depends on tone: said to a cheeky child it's almost affectionate, said to an adult who cheated someone it's a real insult.
Prostituta is the neutral word for prostitute, and trabajadora sexual is used too. Ramera is old and biblical, and used as an insult it means harlot or whore. Puta is the vulgar word.
Porn and pornography. The words themselves are neutral, not swearing; they're here because the topic is for adults. Porno doesn't change for plural or gender: películas porno.
